newsitem.title: INDIA: India protests "assault" on official in Pakistan.
newsitem.headline: India protests "assault" on official in Pakistan.

text.p: India protested to Pakistan on Wednesday over its treatment of a consular official who was accused of spying and expelled last week.

"The Government of India lodges a strong protest against trespass by the intelligence agencies of Pakistan into the residence of Mr A.K. Wahi, the criminal assault on his family, his abduction, illegal detention and injuries inflicted on him as a result of severe beating," said a note handed to Pakistani High Commissioner Riaz Khokhar.
According to the Indian High Commission in Pakistan, a dozen men with knives and a revolver broke into Wahi's home and took him away by force.
Wahi's wife suffered a knife wound on the hand and his teenaged daughter was badly shaken, a High Commission spokesman said.
Wahi, a non-diplomat, was beaten with a rubber tube and suffered bruises all over his back, the spokesman said. He was later released.
"We deplore this kind of incident," senior Foreign Ministry official Vinod Grover told reporters in New Delhi. "It goes beyond any norms of civilised behaviour and diplomatic conduct."
